title: Raw Argo floats and TAO/TRITON moorings agree on 2005-2024 tropical Pacific SST; the RG Argo grid has a 0.1 C warm step in 2016; against raw Argo, DOISST warms 0.06 C/decade too fast in the warm pool
abstract: Question: a campaign study found that after 2013 the gridded Roemmich-Gilson (RG) Argo field warms faster than the West Pacific TAO/TRITON moorings (+0.105 C per decade, 2005-2022). In that study RG supported the warm-pool trend of satellite-type products and the moorings supported in situ products, which changes CERES-era pattern feedbacks by several tenths of a W m-2 K-1. Which observing system shifts, and which products have the correct warm-pool trend? Approach: we used raw data in 10S-10N of the Pacific, 2004-2025: 271,212 Argo profiles (constant depth 3.5-6.5 dbar), 556,970 drifter-days with manufacturer, and daily mooring SST with real-time or delayed-mode codes. We made mooring-Argo, mooring-drifter and Argo-drifter matchups (100 km, 1 day, spatial gradient removed) and compared 2015-2024 with 2005-2013. We sampled seven gridded products at the floats and moorings and calculated trends of their differences. Results: moorings minus floats change by -0.016 C (95% interval -0.038 to +0.008) in the warm pool and -0.004 C in the east (radius range -0.045 to +0.012 C); real-time mooring data have no offset. RG minus the raw floats has a break in February-April 2016 of +0.09 to +0.10 C; against seven references the April 2016 step is +0.07 to +0.17 C and stays after an ENSO control in the warm pool. Newer drifters read warmer: relative to Pacific Gyre, SIO +0.10 C and DBi +0.065 C against both references, so the drifter fleet warmed by about 0.035-0.05 C in 2012-2016. Over 2005-2022, product minus raw Argo trends in the warm pool are RG +0.107, DOISST v2.1 +0.060, OI v2 +0.040, HadISST1 +0.017, HadSST4.2 +0.012, ERSSTv5 -0.009 and COBE-SST2 -0.021 C per decade. Thus the moorings are a valid reference, the post-2013 mooring-Argo conflict is an RG artifact, and raw Argo supports the in situ-type warm-pool trends, not DOISST. Limitations: different measurement depths, few warm-pool moorings after 2017, Argo feeds ERSSTv5 and DOISST, unknown cause of the RG step, tropical Pacific only, and no new feedback calculation.
